hazards.evidence: The caller says the full property "Hotel Quinaçu do Paraúna"; the agent must retain both distinctive components, not reduce it to just "Quinaçu" or confuse with the decoy "Hotel Quinaçu do Paraúna Norte".

hazards.evidence: "Açu" requires ç and an acute accent on A; hearing it alone may not reveal whether the written form is "Açu", "Assu" or another spelling.

hazards.evidence: The supplied distorted forms "Uiraperu" and "Aju" are audibly different from "Uirapuru" and "Açu" in Brazilian Portuguese, creating real capture risk.
hazards.resolving_clarification: "É Uirapuru, com ‘puru’ no final, e Açu com som de ç, não Aju."

hazards.evidence: “Hotel Jacarandá-do-Cerrado” contains the hyphenated compound “Jacarandá-do-Cerrado”; an agent could capture it as separate words, omit one hyphen, or treat “do Cerrado” as a descriptor rather than part of the property name.

hazards.evidence: “Jacarandá” has a final acute accent; the easy controls include some accents, but this hard item combines the accented word with a hyphenated botanical compound.

decisions.comparison_to_easy: Compared with intake_properties_easy_01 “Hotel Vale dos Ipês,” intake_properties_easy_02 “Pousada Ipê Amarelo,” and intake_properties_easy_03 “Pousada Recanto das Andorinhas,” the localized hard value adds a required hyphenated internal boundary and double-R spelling in “Cerrado.” Unlike intake_properties_easy_05 “Hotel Santa Clara,” whose main capture is a simple two-word hotel name, this requires exact spelling of an accented compound property name.
